consensus_summary: Settled consensus centers 'the Way' on Jesus Christ as the exclusive path to the Father (John 14:6) and, by extension, the early Christian movement (Acts) plus the life of discipleship; moral two-ways, Torah-walking, and prophetic highway motifs appear as secondary alternatives.
book_summary: Book defines the term as 'Covenant conduct — the walk,' while noting the common teaching that Jesus is the one way to the Father and the narrow way versus the broad, citing Jer 6:16 and Matt 7:14.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ himself as the exclusive path/means of access to God (with the Christian community and discipleship as extension)
book_core_identification: Covenant conduct, i.e. the walk of obedience
boundary_disagreement: Book demotes the personal-christological identification to a mere 'commonly taught' note and elevates ethical/covenantal walking as the definitional core, whereas consensus treats conduct only as secondary or by-extension.
material_contradiction: Accepting the book's core (the Way = covenant conduct) requires replacing the consensus primary identification (the Way = Jesus Christ); the two cannot both serve as the central referent of the same symbolic term.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: person/path-to-God versus behavioral walk. Although consensus lists moral-path alternatives that overlap with 'the walk,' its settled primary is christological. The book flags that view as common while defining the entry differently, producing a replaced referent rather than a boundary refinement of the same core.
strongest_objection: The 'walk' is already recognized in consensus extensions and alternatives (discipleship, two-ways, walking in God's ways), so the book may only be re-emphasizing an included aspect while still pointing to the Way-Truth-Life chapter.
